Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Manageme.description:
Greenwich College's Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management (SIT60322) is built specifically for international students who want to move into senior management within hospitality, with a particular emphasis on Front of House and Operations rather than the kitchen side of the business. The course trains students in high-level management skills such as managing budgets, developing operational plans and monitoring staff performance, then has them apply those skills to building business plans, marketing strategies and customer service practices they can carry straight into a real venue.

Entry requires completion of Year 10 (or equivalent) plus the Diploma of Hospitality Management, so students arrive with the frontline operational grounding this Advanced Diploma builds on. Greenwich runs the course across five campuses (Sydney, Melbourne, Gold Coast, Perth and Brisbane) over 34 weeks, with a guaranteed vocational placement built into the delivery.

Graduates typically move into hospitality manager, hotel or resort manager, food and beverage manager, operations manager, events manager, front office manager or venue manager roles, or into running their own hospitality business.
Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Manageme.curriculum:
Core units: BSBFIN601 Manage organisational finances, BSBOPS601 Develop and implement business plans, SITXCCS016 Develop and manage quality customer service practices, SITXFIN009 Manage finances within a budget, SITXFIN010 Prepare and monitor budgets, SITXFIN011 Manage physical assets, SITXGLC002 Identify and manage legal risks and comply with the law, SITXHRM009 Lead and manage people, SITXHRM010 Recruit, select and induct staff, SITXHRM012 Monitor staff performance, SITXMGT004 Monitor work operations, SITXMGT005 Establish and conduct business relationships, SITXMPR014 Develop and implement marketing strategies, SITXWHS008 Establish and maintain a work health and safety system.
Elective units (selected from): SITXFSA005 Use hygienic practices for food safety, SITHKOP013 Plan cooking operations, SITHCCC023 Use food preparation equipment, SITHCCC027 to SITHCCC042 (various dish and cookery preparation units covering appetisers, stocks and soups, vegetable and farinaceous dishes, vegetarian and vegan dishes, poultry, meat, seafood, cakes and pastries, dietary requirements, buffets), SITHFAB021 Provide responsible service of alcohol, SITHASC022 Prepare Asian stocks and soups, SITXCOM010 Manage conflict, SITXHRM011 Manage volunteers, SITXHRM008 Roster staff.
Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Manageme.admission_requirements: Successful completion of Australian Year 10 (or equivalent) and the Diploma of Hospitality Management.
Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Manageme.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.

Advanced Diploma of Information Technolo.description:
The Advanced Diploma of Information Technology (ICT60220) is Greenwich College's senior IT qualification, aimed at students who already have foundation-level IT skills and want to move into IT management or specialised technical roles. The course covers networking, IT support, web development and programming, then layers on network security, cloud computing and IT project management, with an emphasis throughout on complex, business-facing problem solving rather than entry-level technical tasks.

Entry requires completion of Year 11 (or equivalent), and Greenwich delivers the course over 104 weeks across its Sydney, Melbourne, Gold Coast and Adelaide campuses, face to face and online.

It's aimed at IT professionals who want to deepen their technical expertise, network and cybersecurity practitioners chasing advanced skills, and help desk or support staff ready to progress into leadership. Typical outcomes are IT manager, network administrator, systems administrator, ICT support manager and entry-to-mid-level cyber security analyst roles.
Advanced Diploma of Information Technolo.curriculum:
Core units: BSBCRT611 Apply critical thinking for complex problem solving, BSBTWK502 Manage team effectiveness, BSBXCS402 Promote workplace cyber security awareness and best practices, ICTICT608 Interact with clients on a business level, ICTICT618 Manage IP, ethics and privacy in ICT environments, ICTSAD609 Plan and monitor business analysis activities in an ICT environment.
Elective units (selected from): ICTCYS608 Perform cyber security risk assessments, ICTCYS612 Design and implement virtualised cyber security infrastructure for organisations, ICTDBS605 Develop knowledge management strategies, ICTICT611 Develop ICT strategic business plans, ICTNWK612 Plan and manage troubleshooting of advanced integrated IP networks, ICTPMG613 Manage ICT project planning, ICTPRG535 Build advanced user interfaces, ICTPRG537 Implement security for applications, ICTPRG605 Manage development of technical solutions from business specifications, ICTSAD611 Manage assessments and validation of ICT solutions.
Advanced Diploma of Information Technolo.admission_requirements: Successful completion of Australian Year 11 or equivalent.
Advanced Diploma of Information Technolo.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.

Advanced Diploma of Leadership and Manag.description:
Greenwich College's Advanced Diploma of Leadership and Management (BSB60420) is pitched at experienced managers and senior team leaders who want to formalise strategic-level leadership skills rather than frontline supervisory ones. The course develops the recruitment, training and team-shaping capabilities needed to run a department, division or whole organisation, alongside strategic planning and organisational performance skills.

Applicants need either a completed Diploma or Advanced Diploma from the BSB Training Package (current or a superseded equivalent version), or two years of full-time equivalent workplace experience in an operational or leadership role. Greenwich runs the 72-week course across Sydney, Melbourne, Perth, Brisbane and the Gold Coast, face to face and online, with up to 10 hours a week of optional learning support.

Graduates typically step into senior manager, operations manager, business manager, general manager (small to medium enterprise) or executive manager roles.
Advanced Diploma of Leadership and Manag.curriculum:
Core units: BSBCRT611 Apply critical thinking for complex problem solving, BSBLDR601 Lead and manage organisational change, BSBLDR602 Provide leadership across the organisation, BSBOPS601 Develop and implement business plans, BSBSTR601 Manage innovation and continuous improvement.
Elective units: BSBPEF501 Manage personal and professional development, BSBPMG633 Provide leadership for the program, BSBSTR602 Develop organisational strategies, BSBPMG637 Engage in collaborative alliance, BSBSUS601 Lead corporate social responsibility.
Advanced Diploma of Leadership and Manag.admission_requirements: Applicants must be 18 years of age or older at course commencement, and must have either completed a Diploma or Advanced Diploma from the BSB Training Package (current or a superseded equivalent version), or completed two years of full-time equivalent relevant workplace experience in an operational or leadership role in an enterprise.
Advanced Diploma of Leadership and Manag.english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (or equivalent), or successful completion of an appropriate Greenwich English course, or successful completion of the Greenwich English placement test.

Advanced Diploma of Marketing automation.description:
Greenwich College's Advanced Diploma of Marketing Automation (11279NAT, CRICOS-listed as "Advanced Diploma of Marketing automation") was developed in partnership with HubSpot and is an 18-month program built specifically around marketing automation rather than general marketing. It goes beyond a typical marketing qualification by combining strategic planning with hands-on practice in the automation platforms employers actually use, aimed at the AI-driven, personalised marketing environment businesses now run in.

Entry requires an Australian Year 12 certificate (or overseas equivalent) at minimum, or any Diploma-level qualification from any training package, or one year of relevant work experience. Greenwich delivers the 76-week course across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide and the Gold Coast, face to face and online.

Graduates typically move into marketing automation specialist, digital marketing manager, CRM and customer engagement manager, martech coordinator or email marketing manager roles.
Advanced Diploma of Marketing automation.curriculum: Units (all core, this is a single accredited course rather than a training-package qualification with electives): NAT11279001 Apply fundamentals of marketing automation, NAT11279002 Implement marketing automation workflows, NAT11279003 Leverage emerging marketing automation technologies for operational efficiency, NAT11279004 Lead the integration of marketing automation, NAT11279005 Implement email and multi-channel marketing automation, NAT11279006 Apply data management practices in marketing automation, NAT11279007 Develop personalised marketing messages using smart content, NAT11279008 Implement regulatory compliance and risk management in marketing automation, NAT11279009 Evaluate marketing automation performance, NAT11279010 Implement digital project management for marketing automation delivery.
Advanced Diploma of Marketing automation.admission_requirements: Completion of an Australian Year 12 certificate or overseas equivalent at a minimum, or completion of any Diploma-level qualification from any training package, or one year of work experience in a relevant field.
Advanced Diploma of Marketing automation.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.

Advanced Diploma of Program Management.description:
The Advanced Diploma of Program Management (BSB60720) trains students to run programs, the large-scale initiatives made up of several dependent projects, rather than a single project in isolation. It covers outlining program objectives, planning execution, managing operations and reporting on status, with the goal of being able to delegate individual projects appropriately while keeping the whole program moving toward business outcomes.

Entry requires a completed Diploma of Project Management (BSB50820, or the earlier BSB51415, including superseded equivalent versions), or two years of full-time equivalent workplace experience at a significant level within a project or program environment. Greenwich runs the 76-week course across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide and the Gold Coast, and includes free access to Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) certification preparation alongside the qualification itself.

Graduates typically move into program manager, senior project manager, portfolio manager, PMO manager or strategic program lead roles.
Advanced Diploma of Program Management.curriculum:
Core units: BSBPMG630 Enable program execution, BSBPMG634 Facilitate stakeholder engagement, BSBPMG635 Implement program governance, BSBPMG636 Manage benefits.
Elective units: BSBPEF502 Develop and use emotional intelligence, BSBPMG631 Manage program delivery, BSBPMG632 Manage program risk, BSBPMG633 Provide leadership for the program, BSBPMG637 Engage in collaborative alliances, BSBLDR601 Lead and manage organisational change, BSBSTR601 Manage innovation and continuous improvement, BSBTWK503 Manage meetings.
Advanced Diploma of Program Management.admission_requirements: Completion of BSB50820 Diploma of Project Management (or the earlier BSB51415 Diploma of Project Management, including a superseded equivalent version), or two years of full-time equivalent relevant workplace experience at a significant level within a project or program environment in an enterprise.
Advanced Diploma of Program Management.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent), or successful completion of an appropriate Greenwich English course, or successful completion of the Greenwich English placement test.

Diploma of Business.description:
Greenwich College's Diploma of Business is currently delivered as the Diploma of Business (Digital Transformation) (BSB50120), reflecting a shift in the course's focus toward the skills corporate and business environments now demand across marketing, finance and logistics. Students gain practical skills in data analysis, Martech automation, SEO, cyber security awareness and content creation, and learn how those pieces work together to build an effective digital strategy and lift a business's overall efficiency.

Entry requires completion of Year 11 (or an overseas equivalent) and applicants must be at least 18. Greenwich delivers the 52-week course across Adelaide, Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane, face to face and online.

It suits professionals wanting to master digital and data skills, marketing professionals building Martech and analytics knowledge, team leaders driving digital projects, and entrepreneurs improving operational efficiency. Typical outcomes are digital transformation officer, digital project coordinator, business transformation analyst, digital strategy coordinator or Martech/marketing automation coordinator roles.
Diploma of Business.curriculum:
Core units: BSBCRT511 Develop critical thinking in others, BSBFIN501 Manage budgets and financial plans, BSBOPS501 Manage business resources, BSBSUS511 Develop workplace policies and procedures for sustainability, BSBXCM501 Lead communication in the workplace.
Elective units: BSBDAT501 Analyse data, BSBINS502 Coordinate data management, BSBTEC403 Apply digital solutions to work processes, BSBXCS402 Promote workplace cyber security awareness and practices, BSBSUS601 Lead corporate social responsibility, BSBCRT412 Articulate, present and debate ideas, BSBTWK503 Manage meetings.
Diploma of Business.admission_requirements: Students must be at least 18 years old and have successfully completed Australian Year 11 or an overseas equivalent.
Diploma of Business.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.

Diploma of Community Services (Case Mana.description:
Greenwich College's Diploma of Community Services (Case Management) (CHC52025) trains students directly in case management practice: coordinating support services, guiding individuals and delivering tailored care to people who need it. It's aimed at students building a career supporting individuals and communities, with an emphasis on empowering people, improving wellbeing and coordinating services across the sector rather than general business or management skills.

Entry requires completion of Year 10 (or overseas equivalent), and Greenwich delivers the 76-week, face-to-face course across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and the Gold Coast.

Graduates typically move into senior youth worker, community development worker (social housing), Aboriginal housing worker, assistant community services worker or case manager roles.
Diploma of Community Services (Case Mana.curriculum:
Core units: HLTWHS003 Maintain work health and safety, CHCLEG003 Manage legal and ethical compliance, CHCDIV001 Work with diverse people, CHCDIV002 Promote Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander cultural safety, CHCDEV005 Analyse impacts of sociological factors on people in community work and services, CHCDFV001 Recognise and respond appropriately to domestic and family violence, CHCCSM017 Facilitate and review case management, CHCMGT005 Facilitate workplace debriefing and support processes, CHCCCS019 Recognise and respond to crisis situations, CHCCCS004 Assess co-existing needs, CHCCCS007 Develop and implement service programs, CHCPRP003 Reflect on and improve own professional practice.
Elective units (selected from): CHCCSM012 Coordinate complex case requirements, CHCCSM014 Provide case management supervision, CHCCSM010 Implement case management practice, CHCCSM016 Undertake advanced assessments, CHCMHS011 Assess and promote social, emotional and physical wellbeing, CHCDIS016 Develop and promote positive person-centred behaviour supports, CHCDIS015 Develop and provide person-centred service responses, CHCCCS009 Facilitate responsible behaviour.
Diploma of Community Services (Case Mana.admission_requirements: Students must have successfully completed Australian Year 10 or an overseas equivalent to Australian Year 10.
Diploma of Community Services (Case Mana.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.

Diploma of E-commerce.description:
Greenwich College markets its Diploma of e-Commerce (11269NAT) as Australia's only accredited diploma of its kind, built specifically around the online business world rather than general marketing or business studies. It covers creating and optimising e-commerce platforms, developing digital marketing strategies for online stores, and managing customer relationships through the post-purchase process.

Entry requires applicants to be at least 18 and to have completed Year 11 (or an overseas equivalent). Greenwich delivers the 52-week course across Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane, face to face and online.

It's aimed at aspiring e-commerce professionals, current business owners expanding their online presence, marketing and sales professionals adding e-commerce skills, and career changers moving into the sector. Typical outcomes are e-commerce coordinator, digital marketing specialist, online sales manager, e-commerce analyst or SEO and web performance officer roles.
Diploma of E-commerce.curriculum: Units (all core, this is a single accredited course rather than a training-package qualification with electives): NAT11269001 Evaluate e-commerce models and operations, NAT11269002 Plan optimisation of the path to purchase in an e-commerce environment, NAT11269003 Create and publish product listings for e-commerce stores, NAT11269004 Implement and optimise the online post-purchase process, NAT11269005 Deliver and enhance customer service practices in an e-commerce environment, NAT11269006 Develop strategies to maximise performance of an e-commerce site, NAT11269007 Apply marketing automation to e-commerce customer communications, NAT11269008 Leverage social media and online communities for e-commerce growth, NAT11269009 Develop paid traffic strategies for online sales, NAT11269010 Develop plans to capitalise on emerging e-commerce opportunities.
Diploma of E-commerce.admission_requirements: Students must be at least 18 years of age and have successfully completed Australian Year 11 or an overseas qualification equivalent to Australian Year 11.
Diploma of E-commerce.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.

Diploma of Early Childhood Education and.description:
Greenwich College's Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care (CHC50125) trains students to design, implement and manage early childhood programs, supporting children's development, leading a team of educators and ensuring compliance with sector standards. It's built for students stepping up from Certificate III level or from other childcare experience into leadership and supervisory roles within a centre.

Entry requires completion of Year 10 (or overseas equivalent). Greenwich delivers the 56-week course across Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane, face to face and online, with practice in purpose-built childcare labs and a guaranteed work placement.

Graduates typically move into lead childcare centre educator, centre manager or coordinator, family day care educator, or kindergarten/preschool assistant roles.
Diploma of Early Childhood Education and.curriculum:
Core units: BSBTWK502 Manage team effectiveness, CHCECE041 Maintain a safe and healthy environment for children, CHCECE042 Foster holistic early childhood learning, development and wellbeing, CHCECE043 Nurture creativity in children, CHCECE044 Facilitate compliance in an education and care service, CHCECE035 Support the holistic learning and development of children, CHCECE045 Foster positive and respectful interactions and behaviour in children, CHCECE046 Implement strategies for the inclusion of all children, CHCECE047 Analyse information to inform children's learning, CHCECE048 Plan and implement children's education and care curriculum, CHCECE049 Embed environmental responsibility in service operations, CHCECE050 Work in partnership with children's families, CHCPRP003 Reflect on and improve own professional practice.
Elective units: CHCMGT003 Lead the work team, BSBPEF502 Develop and use emotional intelligence, BSBHRM413 Support the learning and development of teams and individuals.
Diploma of Early Childhood Education and.admission_requirements: Students must have successfully completed Australian Year 10 or an overseas equivalent to Australian Year 10.
Diploma of Early Childhood Education and.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.

Diploma of Graphic Design.description:
Greenwich College holds CRICOS registration (course code 116132B) for a Diploma of Graphic Design under the national code CUA50720, a 68-week qualification with an estimated total course cost of AU$18,750. Unlike the rest of Greenwich's catalogue, this course currently has no dedicated marketing page on greenwichcollege.edu.au, so this listing draws on the qualification's official government registration data rather than Greenwich's own course-page copy.

CUA50720 reflects the role of practitioners who combine technical, creative and conceptual skills to produce designs that meet client requirements and solve visual communication challenges, working across both print and digital media. Typical job roles associated with the qualification include graphic designer and studio manager, with pathways into related design and creative-industry roles. Note that CUA50720 was marked superseded on the national training register effective 12 August 2025; Greenwich's CRICOS listing has not yet been updated to a successor code as of this review, which may reflect a permitted teach-out period rather than a discontinuation.

Field of education: Creative Arts, Graphic and Design Studies. Course level: Diploma.
Diploma of Graphic Design.curriculum:
Core units (per the CUA50720 national qualification, 9 required): CUAACD531 Refine drawing and other visual representation tools, CUADES413 Develop and extend design skills and practice, CUAGRD501 Research visual communication history and theory, CUAGRD502 Produce graphic designs for 2-D and 3-D applications, CUAGRD503 Produce typographic design solutions, CUAGRD514 Create and manipulate graphics, CUAGRD515 Design and manipulate complex layouts, CUAGRD516 Develop graphic design practice to meet industry needs, CUAPPR513 Present a body of own creative work.
Elective units: 10 additional units are required under the qualification's packaging rules, drawn from a large bank of design, illustration, digital media and business electives (for example CUADES412 Interpret and respond to a design brief, CUAILL401 Develop and refine illustrative work, CUADIG413 Create user interfaces, BSBCRT512 Originate and develop concepts); Greenwich's specific elective selection is not published, since the course currently has no live Greenwich course page.
Diploma of Graphic Design.admission_requirements: No Greenwich-specific published entry requirement is currently available for this course (it has no live course page). Per the national qualification's own entry requirements, applicants must provide evidence of their technical skills and ability to produce multiple examples of graphic design work meeting different design requirements, produce typography that supports the overall design solution, and use graphic design industry software, acquired through personal, work or formal-study experience. Greenwich's general enrolment policy sets Australian Year 10 (or overseas equivalent) as its default academic entry baseline across its VET diplomas.
Diploma of Graphic Design.english_requirements: No Greenwich-specific published English requirement is currently available for this course (it has no live course page). Every other Diploma-level course in Greenwich's current catalogue requires IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent, or an accepted Greenwich English course/placement test result) as a flat, institution-wide figure, so this is very likely the applicable requirement, but it is not confirmed on a course-specific Greenwich page for this qualification.

Diploma of Hospitality Management.description:
Greenwich College's Diploma of Hospitality Management (SIT50422) is aimed at students already working in hospitality (cafes, restaurants, hotels) who want to move into supervisory or management roles, as well as people starting a structured pathway into the industry. The course covers managing budgets and physical assets, leading and rostering staff, monitoring work operations, handling legal risk and compliance, and building customer service and business relationship skills, alongside hands-on food preparation and cookery electives.

Entry requires completion of Year 10 (or equivalent) and the Certificate IV in Kitchen Management. Greenwich delivers the 26-week course across Sydney, Melbourne, Gold Coast, Perth and Brisbane, face to face and online.

Graduates typically move into hospitality manager, hotel or resort manager, food and beverage manager, operations manager, events manager, front office manager or venue manager roles, or into running their own hospitality business.
Diploma of Hospitality Management.curriculum:
Core units: SITXFIN009 Manage finances within a budget, SITXHRM009 Lead and manage people, SITXMGT004 Monitor work operations, SITXCOM010 Manage conflict, SITXWHS007 Implement and monitor work health and safety practices, SITXCCS015 Enhance customer service experiences, SITXCCS016 Develop and manage quality customer service practices, SITXFIN010 Prepare and monitor budgets, SITXGLC002 Identify and manage legal risks and comply with the law, SITXMGT005 Establish and conduct business relationships, SITXHRM008 Roster staff.
Elective units (selected from): SITXFSA005 Use hygienic practices for food safety, SITHKOP013 Plan cooking operations, SITHCCC023 to SITHCCC042 (various dish and cookery preparation units covering appetisers, stocks and soups, vegetable and farinaceous dishes, vegetarian and vegan dishes, poultry, meat, seafood, cakes and pastries, dietary requirements, buffets), SITHFAB021 Provide responsible service of alcohol, SITHASC022 Prepare Asian stocks and soups, SITHCCC039 Produce pates and terrines.
Diploma of Hospitality Management.admission_requirements: Successful completion of Australian Year 10 (or equivalent) and the Certificate IV in Kitchen Management.
Diploma of Hospitality Management.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.

Diploma of Information Technology.description:
Greenwich College's Diploma of Information Technology (ICT50220) is a foundational IT qualification covering programming, web development, databases and software engineering alongside professional employability skills like collaboration, troubleshooting and communication. Students get mentorship from industry professionals through hands-on skill development sessions, and completion leads to one year of credit into the second year of the Bachelor of IT at Greenwich Higher Education (Academy of Interactive Technology Pty Ltd, trading as Greenwich Higher Education, CRICOS 02672K, RTO 91153).

Entry requires completion of Year 11 (or equivalent). Greenwich delivers the course over 60 weeks (48 study weeks across 4 terms plus a 12-week break) at its Sydney and Melbourne campuses only, face to face and online.

It's aimed at people starting out in IT who want foundational coding, web and data skills, and typical outcomes are IT support officer, help desk analyst, junior systems administrator, network support officer or ICT customer support officer roles.
Diploma of Information Technology.curriculum:
Core units (selection): ICTICT517 Match ICT needs with the strategic direction of the organisation, ICTSAD508 Develop technical requirements for business solutions, ICTNWK548 Model preferred system solutions, ICTSAS527 Manage client problems, BSBXTW401 Lead and facilitate a team, BSBCRT512 Originate and develop concepts, ICTWEB522 Develop website information architecture, ICTWEB514 Create dynamic web pages.
Elective units (selection): ICTPRG443 Apply intermediate programming skills in different languages, ICTPRG533 Debug and monitor applications, ICTDAT501 Gather, analyse and verify data from different source inputs, ICTICT532 Apply IP, ethics and privacy in ICT environments, ICTSAD502 Model data processes, ICTDBS506 Design databases, BSBXCS402 Promote workplace cyber security awareness and best practices, ICTWEB451 Apply structured query language in relational databases, ICTPRG444 Analyse software requirements, ICTPRG546 Validate application designs against specifications, ICTPRG532 Apply advanced object oriented language skills, ICTPRG442 Apply mathematical techniques for software development.
Diploma of Information Technology.admission_requirements: Successful completion of Australian Year 11 or equivalent.
Diploma of Information Technology.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.

Diploma of Leadership and Management.description:
Greenwich College's Diploma of Leadership and Management (BSB50420) develops the advanced planning, organising, implementing and monitoring skills needed to run a team successfully, aimed at emerging leaders and current team leaders formalising their skills regardless of prior background or field. It's a step up from supervisory-level training toward coordinator, supervisor or manager-level responsibility.

Entry requires completion of Year 10 (or overseas equivalent). Greenwich delivers the 52-week course across Sydney, Melbourne, Perth, Brisbane and the Gold Coast, face to face and online, with real-world case studies and optional weekly learning support.

Graduates typically move into team leader, supervisor, operations supervisor, business coordinator or project team leader roles.
Diploma of Leadership and Management.curriculum:
Core units: BSBCMM511 Communicate with influence, BSBCRT511 Develop critical thinking in others, BSBLDR523 Lead and manage effective workplace relationships, BSBOPS502 Manage business operational plans, BSBPEF502 Develop and use emotional intelligence.
Elective units: BSBOPS505 Manage organisational customer service, BSBSTR502 Facilitate continuous improvement, BSBSUS511 Develop workplace policies and procedures for sustainability, BSBTWK503 Manage meetings, BSBXCM501 Lead communication in the workplace, BSBDAT501 Analyse data.
Diploma of Leadership and Management.admission_requirements: Students must have successfully completed Australian Year 10 or an overseas equivalent to Australian Year 10.
Diploma of Leadership and Management.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.

Diploma of Marketing and Communication.description:
Greenwich College's Diploma of Marketing and Communication (BSB50620) builds digital marketing and social media skills for the marketing communications industry, covering communication, marketing concepts, media planning, social media and budgets. It's aimed at emerging leaders and current supervisors who want to develop stronger leadership and team engagement skills alongside their marketing expertise.

Entry requires either the BSB42415 Certificate IV in Marketing and Communication, or completion of six named foundation units (Make presentations, Articulate present and debate ideas, Undertake marketing activities, Analyse consumer behaviour, Develop and apply knowledge of communications industry, Write complex documents) or their mapped equivalents, or two years of full-time equivalent relevant work experience. Greenwich delivers the 52-week course across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and the Gold Coast, face to face and online.

Graduates typically move into marketing manager, marketing team leader, communications leader or brand/product manager roles.
Diploma of Marketing and Communication.curriculum:
Core units: BSBMKG541 Identify and evaluate marketing opportunities, BSBMKG542 Establish and monitor the marketing mix, BSBMKG552 Design and develop marketing communication plans, BSBMKG555 Write persuasive copy, BSBPMG430 Undertake project work.
Elective units: BSBMKG543 Plan and interpret market research, BSBMKG545 Conduct marketing audits, BSBMKG551 Create multiplatform advertisements for mass media, BSBCMM511 Communicate with influence, BSBPEF501 Manage personal and professional development, BSBOPS501 Manage business resources, BSBPMG535 Manage project information and communication.
Diploma of Marketing and Communication.admission_requirements: Completion of BSB42415 Certificate IV in Marketing and Communication, or completion of BSBCMM411 Make presentations, BSBCRT412 Articulate present and debate ideas, BSBMKG433 Undertake marketing activities, BSBMKG435 Analyse consumer behaviour, BSBMKG439 Develop and apply knowledge of communications industry and BSBWRT411 Write complex documents (or mapped equivalent competencies), or two years of full-time equivalent relevant work experience.
Diploma of Marketing and Communication.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.

Diploma of Project Management.description:
Greenwich College's Diploma of Project Management (BSB50820) trains students to lead a project through its full lifecycle, from setting and tracking budgets to managing development, controlling communication and managing human resources. It's aimed at professionals currently managing projects who want to formalise their skills, project coordinators moving into full project management roles, and team leaders responsible for budgets, timelines and stakeholder communication.

Entry requires completion of Year 10 (or overseas equivalent). Greenwich runs the 52-week course across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide and the Gold Coast, and includes access to Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) certification preparation.

Graduates typically move into project manager, project coordinator, project team leader, project officer or program support officer roles.
Diploma of Project Management.curriculum:
Core units: BSBPMG530 Manage project scope, BSBPMG531 Manage project time, BSBPMG532 Manage project quality, BSBPMG533 Manage project cost, BSBPMG534 Manage project human resources, BSBPMG535 Manage project information and communication, BSBPMG536 Manage project risk, BSBPMG540 Manage project integration.
Elective units: BSBCMM511 Communicate with influence, BSBSTR502 Facilitate continuous improvement, BSBSUS511 Develop workplace policies and procedures for sustainability, BSBTWK502 Manage team effectiveness.
Diploma of Project Management.admission_requirements: Students must have successfully completed Australian Year 10 or an overseas equivalent to Australian Year 10.
Diploma of Project Management.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.

Graduate Diploma of Management (Learning.description:
Greenwich College's Graduate Diploma of Management (Learning) (BSB80120) is a VET qualification delivered under the nationally recognised BSB Training Package rather than a higher-education award, despite the "Graduate Diploma" title. It's aimed at leaders and managers who need to build flexibility and adaptability into their practice, with a specific focus on organisational learning and development strategy, strategic transformation and innovative leadership thinking.

Entry requires completion of Year 12 (or overseas equivalent) at minimum, plus either completion of an AQF level 5 (Diploma-level) qualification in Australia or overseas, or at least one year of full-time equivalent relevant workplace experience in an operational, leadership or management role. Greenwich delivers the 68-week course across Sydney, Melbourne, Perth and Brisbane, face to face and online.

Graduates typically move into operations manager, business manager, team leader/supervisor, project manager or department manager roles.
Graduate Diploma of Management (Learning.curriculum:
Core units: BSBHRM613 Contribute to the development of learning and development strategies, TAELED803 Implement improved learning practice, BSBLDR811 Lead strategic transformation.
Elective units: BSBSTR801 Lead innovative thinking and practice, BSBTWK601 Develop and maintain strategic business networks, BSBHRM611 Contribute to organisational performance development, BSBLDR812 Develop and cultivate collaborative partnerships and relationships, BSBTEC601 Review organisational digital strategy.
Graduate Diploma of Management (Learning.admission_requirements: Students must have successfully completed Australian Year 12 or an overseas equivalent at minimum, and completion of an AQF level 5 (Diploma-level qualification) or higher in Australia or an overseas equivalent, or at least 1.0 years of full-time equivalent relevant workplace experience in an operational, leadership or management role.
Graduate Diploma of Management (Learning.english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 overall (or equivalent). Successful completion of an appropriate level of a Greenwich English course or the Greenwich English placement test is also accepted.
